name: Color Moment Invariant Analysis
description: Computes rotation- and scale-invariant color moments to characterize the color distribution of an image in a compact, transformation-independent representation. Natural photographs exhibit color moment patterns constrained by physical scene statistics, while AI-generated images produce characteristic deviations in their higher-order color moments.
algorithm: Hu-Derived Color Moment Invariants + Distribution Divergence Scoring
mechanism:
Color moments provide a compact statistical representation of color distributions: the first moment (mean) captures the average color, the second (variance) captures spread, and the third (skewness) captures asymmetry. By computing these moments independently in each channel (H, S, V or L, a, b) and combining them with Hu's moment invariants, the result is a feature vector that is invariant to rotation and scaling — capturing the intrinsic color distribution properties regardless of image orientation.

The forensic application exploits the fact that natural scene color distributions follow predictable statistical constraints: (1) **Skewness patterns** — outdoor scenes typically have positively skewed luminance (more dark pixels than bright); AI generators often produce near-symmetric distributions. (2) **Inter-channel moment correlations** — in natural images, the a* and b* channel moments in CIELAB space are correlated due to physical reflectance properties of natural materials; AI images frequently violate these correlations. (3) **Moment stability across scales** — in natural images, color moments computed at multiple resolutions show smooth, predictable decay; AI images exhibit erratic multi-scale behavior.

The 9-dimensional moment feature vector (3 moments × 3 channels) is compared against reference distributions using the Mahalanobis distance to produce an anomaly score.
parameters:
Color space: CIELAB (L*, a*, b*) or HSV
Moments computed: mean (μ), variance (σ²), skewness (γ)
Feature vector: 9D (3 channels × 3 moments)
Invariants: Hu moments 1-4 on each channel
Multi-scale: 3 levels (1×, 0.5×, 0.25×)
Decision: Mahalanobis distance from natural image centroid
accuracy: Low to Moderate — 58-70% standalone accuracy. Color moments capture coarse distributional properties and are most useful as fast screening features in a larger ensemble.
source: Mindru, F. et al. (2004). Moment Invariants for Recognition under Changing Viewpoint and Illumination. CVIU.
useCase: Fast screening of suspected AI-generated images based on color distribution anomalies, rotation/scale-invariant content matching for forensic image retrieval, detecting images with artificially balanced or manipulated color palettes, and providing baseline color features for ensemble forensic classifiers.
strengths:
• Rotation and scale invariance makes analysis independent of image orientation and resolution
• 9-dimensional feature vector provides an extremely compact image signature
• Computation is trivially fast — simple statistical aggregation over pixel values
• The inter-channel moment correlation test exploits physical constraints of natural materials
limitations:
• Color moments are coarse descriptors — many different images can share similar moment vectors
• Low standalone accuracy — must be combined with spatial/frequency methods for reliable detection
• Color post-processing (saturation boost, color grading) alters moments of authentic images
• Monochromatic or low-saturation images provide insufficient variation for meaningful moment analysis

references.title: Mindru, F. et al. (2004). Moment Invariants for Recognition under Changing Viewpoint and Illumination. CVIU.
Stricker, M.A. & Orengo, M. (1995). Similarity of Color Images. SPIE Storage and Retrieval.
